limitations: Full training stdout, TensorBoard scalars and frozen config are now available and checked. They still contain no cumulative push-event, invalid-injection, per-stratum training exposure, pre/post velocity trace or event-dwell counter.

Episode-length scalars are logged averages, not unique episode/event records. Counts of log points above a schedule threshold are indirect survival coverage only; overlapping logging windows cannot produce an event count or confidence interval.
Framework command metric telemetry is sampled during stochastic PPO training and is separate from deterministic formal evaluation and the task-owned recovery classifier.

The exact target logger implementation / averaging-window definition for Train/mean_episode_length and Train/mean_reward was not among these downloaded sources; the audit reports recorded scalar values without treating each as an independent episode sample.
scope_note: Go2 formal 832/832 recovered and G1 0/832 recovered are separate evaluated policy outcomes. Go2 reference NO-GO is caused by upper headroom gate, not poor task score. No reward/protocol changes or new experiment are made here.

supplement.purpose: Original 500-iteration stdout/env.yaml/agent.yaml/TensorBoard and precise framework source audit; replaces initial local-availability limitations only.
supplement.scalar_read_method: Independently decode TFRecord Event/Summary simple_value floats from downloaded bytes with Python stdlib; all 18 tags per robot match inventory count/first3/last10 exactly. No TensorBoard package installed or GPU used.

framework_step_order.finding: Increment episode_length_buf after physics; termination_manager.compute then reward_manager.compute(step_dt).
Reset terminated environments, update commands, then apply interval events.
Subtract dt from per-env timer; when below 1e-6, invoke configured event on valid_env_ids and resample interval. With fixed .02 interval and .02 control dt it is evaluated every control step.
Each full_program output is multiplied by weight and dt once; per-episode accumulation uses this integrated value. No upstream reward terms are active in downloaded env config.
Episode_Reward/full_program logs mean accumulated integrated reward divided by max_episode_length_s; it is not the raw instantaneous reward or recovery rate.

tensorboard_success_metric.semantics: UniformVelocityCommand accumulates actual body-frame XY norm and absolute body-yaw velocity tracking error; at reset it thresholds their per-episode means and writes Metrics/success_rate.
tensorboard_success_metric.interpretation: This inherited locomotion telemetry must not be called Push recovery success. Both robots reach 0 late in stochastic training, although Go2 deterministic formal eval recovers 832/832.

training_trend_interpretation: G1 episode length and logged return improve strongly, while mean body yaw-rate tracking error remains large and rises late. This is consistent with survival/upright reward gains coexisting with rotational motion, rather than successful stationary recovery.

Policy/mean_std increases in both robots (G1 1.0023 to 2.0084; Go2 1.0020 to 2.2421). These are policy distribution standard deviations, not physical angular velocities or recovery rates; this shared trend does not alone explain the divergent deterministic evaluation outcomes.
No causal claim about a particular reward term or entropy coefficient is established by these observational logs. No reward/protocol edits or retraining were performed.
